about: Toolchain layers: Debian packages prebuilt on top of the streamed base rootfs (docs/DEBIAN.md "Toolchain layers"). scripts/debian/build-layers.sh builds them; src/debian/layers.ts applies them; `toolchain install ID` applies one.

c.title: C and C++
c.description: gcc, g++, make, cmake, gdb, pkg-config (build-essential)

python.title: Python 3
python.description: python3, pip, venv, dev headers, numpy, requests, yaml, tkinter (turtle draws in an X11 window)
python.check: python3 -c 'import json, venv, numpy, tkinter, turtle; print(json.dumps([1]))'

classic.title: Classic languages
prepare: # Every program cobc builds printed "Warning: program compiled against libxml 212 using older 209"
# (#110). trixie has one libxml2, 2.12.7+dfsg+really2.9.14: the 2.9.14 library under a 2.12.7
# version number. Debian's libcob4t64 3.2-3 was compiled while the archive had the real 2.12.7
# and was not rebuilt, so cob_init calls xmlCheckVersion(21207) and the library answers 20914.
# No package in trixie fixes that, so the version libcob asks for (mov $21207,%edi before each
# of its two calls) becomes the one installed. Only with exactly that libxml2 and exactly two
# such calls; otherwise libcob stays as Debian built it. dpkg --verify libcob4t64 shows the change.
lib=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu

if [ -e $lib/libxml2.so.2.9.14 ] && [ -f $lib/libcob.so.4.2.0 ]; then perl -e 'my $f = shift; open(my $h, "+<:raw", $f) or die "$f: $!"; local $/; my $d = <$h>; my $old = "\xbf\xd7\x52\x00\x00\xe8"; my $new = "\xbf\xb2\x51\x00\x00\xe8"; my $n = () = $d =~ /\Q$old\E/g; if ($n != 2) { print "libcob: $n xmlCheckVersion(21207) calls, not 2: left as it is\n"; exit 0 } $d =~ s/\Q$old\E/$new/g; seek($h, 0, 0); print $h $d; close($h) or die "$f: $!"; print "libcob: xmlCheckVersion(21207) is now xmlCheckVersion(20914), twice\n"' $lib/libcob.so.4.2.0; else echo 'libcob: not the libxml2 2.9.14 this was written for: left as it is'; fi

go.title: Go
go.description: Debian's golang-go, with the standard library already compiled
prepare: # std compiled into the default build cache of the tab's user (HOME=/home/user), so
# go build in the tab only compiles the user's packages
mkdir -p /home/user/.cache
env HOME=/home/user CGO_ENABLED=0 go build std
# go deletes cache entries whose mtime is over 5 days old (and ignores a trim.txt
# dated in the future), so the entries themselves are dated 2100: never trimmed,
# never re-touched (build-layers.sh leaves such times unclamped)
rm -f /home/user/.cache/go-build/trim.txt
find /home/user/.cache/go-build -type f -exec touch -d @4102444800 {} +
# cgo off (the PATH's cc is tabcomputer's WASM compiler; the cache above is built
# without cgo) and one build job at a time: Blink runs one guest thread anyway, and
# parallel forks can wedge go until Blink's vfork stops taking Go's SIGURG.
# go env -w writes this file; go env -u NAME undoes a setting
mkdir -p /home/user/.config/go && printf 'CGO_ENABLED=0\nGOFLAGS=-p=1\n' > /home/user/.config/go/env
go.check:
printf 'package main
import "fmt"
func main(){fmt.Println("hello")}
' > /tmp/tc-hello.go && cd /tmp && go run tc-hello.go

rescue.title: File rescue
rescue.description: converters for dead formats: WordPerfect, Publisher, Works, Lotus 1-2-3, ClarisWorks and old Mac files, Access (mdbtools), and pandoc
rescue.check: command -v wpd2html pub2xhtml wps2html wks2csv mwaw2html mdb-export > /dev/null && pandoc --version | head -n 1

tex-full.title: LaTeX, full
tex-full.description: tex plus TikZ, biblatex and biber, latex-extra, science, the extra fonts, XeTeX and LuaTeX
tex-full.check: kpsewhich tikz.sty biblatex.sty siunitx.sty xpatch.sty fourier.sty && xelatex --version | head -n 1 && biber --version
